title: God Comes, with Succor Speedy
description: God Comes, with Succor Speedy in Tonic Solfa to AURELIA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 596, “Lo! He Cometh”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6 D) (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AURELIA; any other Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6 D) tune fits them as well.
underlay: God comes, with suc-cor spee-dy, To those who suf-fer wrong; To help the poor and nee-dy, And bid the weak be strong; He comes to break op-pres-sion, And set the cap-tive free, To take a-way trans-gres-sion, And rule in eq-ui-ty.

lines: To help the poor and needy,
And bid the weak be strong;
He shall come down, as showers
And joy and hope, like flowers,
Spring in His path to birth.
The tide of time shall never
His great, best name of Love.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to AURELIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
